page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 12 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM. The processing unit is based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing AMD EPYC 9575F processors running at 2.0 GHz with 12 physical cores and a shared CPU allocation. The system features a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be attached. It runs on the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores also rank in the top 10%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, falls into the average to strong categories. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong, while write bandwidth and small-block read bandwidth remain average. For machine learning tasks, LLM inference text generation using a small 135M model reaches top-tier speeds, though prompt processing for the same model is average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers a high density of memory relative to CPU cores, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core alongside dedicated GPU acceleration. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring GPU-compute capabilities without the high overhead of larger multi-GPU instances. The lack of local storage requires users to factor in the latency of network-attached storage. Suitable workloads include small-scale LLM inference, image processing, graphics rendering, and memory-intensive data processing tasks that leverage GPU acceleration.
